what_this_is: Golden-set drifts a person has read and decided about. It exists because between 26 and 31 August 2026 the Signal golden set failed six consecutive full runs, an email went out every time, and nothing was done about any of them. The check was correct on all six. What was missing was anywhere to write down 'we looked at this, here is what we decided, and here is what would change it' — so every run reported the same unactioned drift as if it were news, and the signal was lost in its own repetition. whatholdsup has draft_decisions.json for exactly this; Signal had nothing.
how_to_use_it: A decision is keyed on slug + category + the direction of the move. Record one only after reading the claims. A decision does NOT silence the category: a drift in a NEW direction, or a new category, still fails. It only stops a judgment you have already made from failing again.
the_hard_case: A decision of 'fixture_is_right' means the model is wrong and the baseline stays. Those categories will keep failing until the mapping improves, and that is correct — but they must be visible as KNOWN and separated from drifts nobody has looked at, or you are back where you started.

decisions.reason: Seven claims, and every substantive one says the modalities are comparable: transfusion independence RR 1.04 (95% CI 0.91-1.19), no statistically significant difference in vaso-occlusive crisis reduction between exa-cel and lentiviral therapies, similar engraftment and neutrophil recovery, comparable or superior fetal haemoglobin induction. There is no second side — no claim holds that either modality outperforms the other. The one caveat claim says no head-to-head randomised trial exists and indirect comparison is limited; that is a statement about EVIDENCE QUALITY, not a competing position, and treating it as one is what produced the old 'debated' label. The single aplasia-event claim compares two CRISPR approaches to each other, not CRISPR to lentiviral.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A claim entering the corpus that asserts one modality is superior, or a head-to-head trial reporting a difference.

decisions.action: NOT re-baselined. This category will keep failing until the mapping improves.
decisions.reason: Five of six claims converge on FINDINGS — CD4+/CD8+ T-lymphocyte and macrophage infiltration, no eosinophilic infiltrate, no spike protein detected in myocardial tissue, a histopathological pattern distinct from viral myocarditis, and late gadolinium enhancement on MRI. The sixth says mechanisms remain 'proposed' and names three competing candidates: molecular mimicry between spike protein and cardiac myosin, mRNA-induced immune activation, and hypersensitivity reactions — the last of which claim 2 arguably rules out. The category asks what the mechanism IS. That is unsettled and the claims say so. The model read agreement about observations as agreement about mechanism, which is the conflation of four different things measured and reported as one.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Claims entering the corpus that settle on one mechanism, or the mapping learning to separate agreement about findings from agreement about explanations.

decisions.action: re-baselined 2026-08-31, under the minority-dispute rule below
decisions.decided_by: Fred Ugast (editorial rule); claude (claims read at source)
decisions.reason: 35 of 41 claims are uncontested trial results and epidemiology, but a real dispute sits inside them: ribociclib showed overall-survival benefit across MONALEESA-2, -3 and -7 and MONARCH-2 reached significance, while PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3 did not. Whether all CDK4/6 inhibitors extend life is genuinely unsettled and is the subject of What Holds Up issue two. Under the standing rule recorded below, a real minority dispute makes the category debated. So 'debated' is correct and the model was right. SEPARATELY AND STILL OPEN: two claims in this category contradict each other on PALOMA-3 — one gives OS HR 0.81 at p=0.0221, the other says PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3 showed numerical but not statistically significant benefit. One of them is wrong. That is a corpus defect, not a mapping question, and re-baselining does not fix it.
decisions.what_would_change_it: The minority-dispute rule changing. The PALOMA-3 contradiction is outstanding regardless and should be resolved in the corpus.

open_instrument_finding.what: THE ALIAS MOVES, AND IT MOVED WITHIN THREE HOURS. The 13:00 UTC scheduled run and two local runs a few hours later disagreed on three categories — breast-cancer-therapies/treatment_selection, mrna-vaccine-myocarditis/clinical_outcomes_and_severity, and social-media-teen-mental-health/methodology, whose side balance reversed [10,3] -> [3,8] while its published label stayed 'debated'. Everything else was held constant and checked: identical claim corpus (207/205/2, 136/134/2, 130/130/0, 211/202/9 — matching CI exactly), same fixture, no SIGNAL_MODEL override in .env or CI, no commit touching map_consensus.py, signal_model.py, topic_config.py or score_claims.py, and temperature=0 with no caching and no seed. Deterministic decoding on identical inputs produced different judgments three hours apart.
open_instrument_finding.why_it_matters: This is the failure golden_set.py was built for and its docstring predicts: 'no dated snapshot is published for it... Judgments can move without a code change.' Last time the detection window was five months. This time it was three hours. It also means those three categories cannot be fixed by re-baselining — record today and tomorrow goes red on a different three.
open_instrument_finding.not_yet_confirmed: The conclusion 'the alias moved' is reached by elimination, not observation. The confirming test is to re-run those four topics after a gap: a FOURTH distinct result means continuous drift and no baseline can hold for any of the 53; a match with today's local pair means it moved once and settled.
open_instrument_finding.consequence_for_whatholdsup: The whatholdsup gate binds every verdict to the sha it judged, which is right, and records model 'claude-sonnet-4-6', which is an alias and therefore does not identify what actually judged. Its --since optimisation carries claim verdicts forward from earlier runs to save money. If the model can move in three hours, a carried verdict was produced by a judge that may no longer exist. Any measurement taken through a model role — including the fatal-class recall baseline of 2026-08-31 — has a shelf life. Deterministic checks do not.
open_instrument_finding.confirmed_2026_08_31: FOUR observations now: the 13:00 UTC CI run, two local passes minutes apart, and a third pass hours later. TWO categories drift in every one — breast-cancer/survival_outcomes and mrna-myocarditis/biological_mechanism. THREE flicker: treatment_selection drifted in the two back-to-back local passes and in neither CI nor the later pass; clinical_outcomes_and_severity and the social-media/methodology side reversal appeared in CI alone. Three observations, three different sets. So it is not 'the alias moved once and settled' — within a short window the pipeline is deterministic, and across hours the result flickers. The two stable drifts are real and have been decided. The three flickering ones cannot be fixed by re-baselining: record one and the next run goes red on whichever way the coin lands. They need the mapping to stop sitting on the boundary, which R-01 above may itself help with by writing the threshold down.

standing_rules.rule: A real but minority dispute inside a category makes that category DEBATED, not consensus.
standing_rules.in_his_words: A real but minority dispute does make a 41 claim category debated. Many times a minority turns out to be more right than wrong. At some level there might be a case where we judge the minority too small or undercredentialed to take seriously, but that should be pretty rare for our purposes.
standing_rules.why: An evidence assessment that rounds minority positions away is doing the thing it exists to criticise. The cost of calling a genuine dispute 'consensus' is that a reader is told the question is closed when it is not; the cost of the reverse is only that they are told to look closer.
consequences_not_yet_acted_on: THE RULE BELONGS IN THE MAPPING PROMPT, not only here. Until it is in _build_category_prompt the model applies its own unwritten threshold and every category gets adjudicated one at a time, forever. Editing that file triggers a full 53-category run, which is the right price for a rule change.

CONSENSUS SHOULD GET RARER. 47 of 53 categories currently read consensus. If a genuine minority dispute is enough, some of those 47 are mislabelled — and the label flips we have been chasing may partly be the model wobbling around a threshold nobody had ever written down. Worth one deliberate sweep after the rule is in the prompt, rather than discovering it through failing runs.
